target_customer: Nonprofit organizations that need fundraising, donor, volunteer and event management in one system
problem: Small and mid-sized nonprofits juggled separate tools for donations, donors, volunteers and events, while incumbents were costly and complex.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for nonprofits plus onboarding and data migration services
product_category: All-in-one nonprofit CRM and fundraising software

founders.name: Allan Shin
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls the founders Canadian twins.

founders.name: Anisa Mirza
founders.background_notes: Not listed on the current YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web CRM with payments, events and volunteer modules is standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Donor data and integrated workflows are costly to migrate, but features were available from many nonprofit vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition of Giveffect found; the sector consolidated, for example SofterWare acquired Givecloud in January 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch described the 2015 pitch as Shopify meets Salesforce for nonprofits, implying demand for simpler all in one tools versus legacy systems.

branding.domain_note: Uses giveffect.com, an exact name match.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and upbeat with wordplay, such as 'We Giveffect about you.'

brand_strength.rationale: A give plus effect coinage that is often misspelled as Giveeffect, with a registered word mark but no sourced community or brand press.

outcome_analysis: Giveffect has stayed independent and active more than a decade after YC Winter 2015, selling all in one software to nonprofits with partnerships such as Double the Donation. No public round beyond YC is verified, and growth versus Blackbaud and other consolidating vendors is unknown, so it looks like a durable niche software business rather than a venture-scale outlier, though revenue is not public.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights shows a 120K seed (Feb 2015) from YC; Bouncewatch 8.83M total incl. 8.7M in Jan 2017; Village.ai 12M total; zerogtalent 500K. All aggregators, none recorded. Competitor list empty: the search returned only 2023 to 2026 pages. Success factor capital_efficiency is an inference from survival without a visible raise and is weakly supported. Team size is blank in the dataset; a September 2022 press release shows a software grant program. Completeness pass: the 120K seed is recorded from CB Insights alone (single database). Bouncewatch reports 8.83M in total including 8.7M in 2017-01, which conflicts and is not recorded.
